body: India's SME platforms (BSE SME, NSE Emerge) saw a boom in 2023-24 with tiny issues oversubscribed hundreds of times. Cases: Varanium Cloud (NSE Emerge; raised Rs 40 cr in 2022 for data centres/learning centres, stock rallied many-fold) -- SEBI interim order May 2024 barred it and its promoter for inflated revenues and misuse of IPO money; Add-Shop E-Retail -- SEBI found manipulated financials to fuel the share price (2024); Resourceful Automobile (Aug 2024): a Rs 12 cr IPO for a two-showroom dealer oversubscribed ~400x drew public criticism; DroneAcharya (BSE SME) -- SEBI order (28 Nov 2025) fined the company/promoters Rs 75 lakh and barred them for up to two years for booking Rs 12.35 cr of income from entities that received no goods/services and inflating FY24 profits (company appealing); FOCL-linked SME IPOs -- SEBI found up to ~Rs 100 cr of IPO fund diversion (2025). SEBI tightened rules in 2025 (profitability track record, OFS limits, curbs on general corporate purposes; NSE capped listing-day gains). Visible flags: sudden revenue/profit jump in the 1-2 years pre-IPO; related-party customers/vendors; tiny float and extreme subscription; same merchant bankers across many problem issues; bonus/split + preferential allotments after listing; promoters exiting after lock-in; Telegram/WhatsApp tips. Lesson: treat SME IPOs as guilty until proven innocent; require multi-year audited CFO, check banker's past listings, and avoid on circuit-filter-driven price runs.

data.early_signals: pre-IPO revenue spike; related-party sales; banker track record; extreme oversubscription; post-listing bonus/preferential
data.lesson: SME IPOs: assume promoter-driven pricing; verify CFO
data.spotted_by: SEBI forensic audits; Value Research, journalists

title: SME IPO manipulation wave (2024-2025)
